ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small ball is thrown horizontally. A stroboscope and camera are used to photograph the motion of the ball, with the stroboscope flashing every 0.05s. During one particular shot, the stroboscope flashes precisely at the instant the ball is thrown. The photograph, after editing, is shown in the figure. The first ball in the figure is the image at the instant of being thrown, and 3 images are removed between every two adjacent balls. The ratio of the lengths of the two line segments $s_{1}$ and $s_{2}$ as indicated is 3:7. The magnitude of the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and air resistance is neglected.

1. Determine the magnitude of the velocity of the ball at the instant it is thrown.

The ratio of the lengths of the two line segments $s_1$ and $s_2$ as indicated is 3:7. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three retained images of the small ball, arranged along a blue dashed parabolic path that curves toward the lower right; the leftmost small ball is close to the hand, and is the position at the instant of throwing. The s1 marked in the figure is the straight-line segment from the first small ball to the second small ball, and s2 is the straight-line segment from the second small ball to the third small ball. Reasoning: The stroboscopic period is 0.05 s, and between every two adjacent visible small balls 3 intermediate images have been deleted, so the time interval between adjacent visible images is T = 4 × 0.05 s = 0.20 s. The ball is thrown horizontally; taking vertically downward as positive, then the displacement in the first displayed time interval is (v0 T, (1/2)gT^2), the horizontal displacement in the second displayed time interval is still v0 T, while the vertical displacement is (1/2)g(2T)^2 - (1/2)gT^2 = (3/2)gT^2. Therefore |s1| = sqrt((v0T)^2 + ((1/2)gT^2)^2), |s2| = sqrt((v0T)^2 + ((3/2)gT^2)^2). From the given |s1|:|s2| = 3:7, obtain sqrt((v0T)^2 + ((1/2)gT^2)^2) / sqrt((v0T)^2 + ((3/2)gT^2)^2) = 3/7. Substituting g = 10 m/s^2, T = 0.20 s, there are (1/2)gT^2 = 0.2 m, (3/2)gT^2 = 0.6 m. Let x = v0T, then (x^2 + 0.2^2)/(x^2 + 0.6^2) = 9/49, that is, 49(x^2+0.04)=9(x^2+0.36), solving gives 40x^2 = 1.28, x^2 = 0.032. Thus v0 = x/T = sqrt(0.032)/0.20 = sqrt(0.8) = 2sqrt(5)/5 m/s.
